Definition: Caphtor (i.e. a wreath-shaped island), the original seat of the Philistines
BiblicalUsage: Caphtor is the original home of the Philistines, the island or coastland from which they came to the shores of Canaan. Amos says the Philistines came from Caphtor as Israel came from Egypt; Deuteronomy says the Caphtorims destroyed the Avims and dwelt in their stead; and Jeremiah says the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Caphtor reminds me that God moves nations as He moved Israel: the Philistines had their own exodus, and the God who brought Israel out of Egypt also brought them out of Caphtor.
